items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Sets Nintendo Switch 2 Release Date for Early August
items.summary: "We're very happy to bring this to you."
items.content: Square Enix has announced Final Fantasy 14 has a Nintendo Switch 2 release date of August 4, 2026. More like this Open Back Headphones: A Sound Experience Like No Other Game director Naoki Yoshida (a.k.a. Yoshi-P) suited up in Bastion armor and took the stage at Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin to confirm the news alongside a laundry list of new updates coming in the near future. While Square Enix had previously confirmed plans to bring FFXIV to Switch 2 in August, today's news locks in a launch that's only a little more than one week away.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV comes to Switch 2 Aug. 4th, 2026, new Evercold trailers shared
items.content:
0 Square Enix recently announced that Final Fantasy XIV is coming to Switch 2 in August 2026. Now we have an official release date for the Switch 2 version, and it’s not far away: August 4th, 2026. The game will require a subscription fee (as it does on other platforms), but Switch Online won’t be necessary to play. You can see all the details now on the Switch eShop . You may want to clear some space out now, because this one will be 117GB at launch on Switch 2.

In addition, we know that Switch 2 will be getting the new Evercold expansion when it launches in January 2027. Today we have multiple new looks at the Evercold content. You can see an extended teaser trailer above to get a broad overview. Check out the bottom of this post for more in depth looks at brand new areas to explore, the new Bastion class, and the upcoming collab with Evangelion.

In the time of the Ancients, Etheirys was divided across ten and three reflections to avert a terrible calamity. Thus, for twelve thousand years did the star survive, and by its enduring hope did the Warrior of Light at last thwart its Final Days. Yet victory comes at a cost, and fate now demands its due.

Faced with the new threat of the Solstice, the Warrior of Light is summoned to the Fourth reflection. But what do they hope to gain from wandering a world lost to ice? Hold fast to your convictions and join with your comrades as you brave the ever-expanding world of FINAL FANTASY XIV!

items.title: More Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold Screenshots, Art Released
Final Fantasy XIV’s latest live letter gave us a detailed preview of the Beastmaster coming in September
items.summary: The start of September is when Final Fantasy XIV players will get to enjoy the second limited job added to the game, Beastmaster, but this weekend's fan festival had more to show off than just the next expansion. The latest live letter from the producer was an extended preview of Beastmaster's gameplay, showing off how the [...]
items.content:
The start of September is when Final Fantasy XIV players will get to enjoy the second limited job added to the game, Beastmaster, but this weekend’s fan festival had more to show off than just the next expansion. The latest live letter from the producer was an extended preview of Beastmaster’s gameplay, showing off how the job summons its different companions and then unleashes companion skills to form combination attacks with the master. These combinations can be executed in succession for an increasingly powerful sequence of attacks, as well as allowing the master to borrow an ability and unleash it at will.

The Beastmaster’s Crucible of the Unbroken was also demonstrated, which works as something of a limited roguelike mode within the game that will start becoming a dominant element of play after level 30. Players progress through nodes containing battles, recovery, and various mode-specific items; your HP doesn’t automatically recover, which means that you have to carefully manage health for both your character and pets while managing affinities and weaknesses. The Crucible also allows you to rank up your partners (including unlocking new appearances) and challenge more difficult versions of the mode. Players can even compete for high scores in the ranking, with rewards for higher-ranked players. We’ve included a shot-by-shot summary thread below for recaps.

To recap quickly, the Beastmaster limited job can be unlocked by having a combat job at 50 or above, complete the 2.0 main scenario, and register the Dawntrail expansion to your account.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold's first new job is Bastion
items.summary: Everything from the keynote at Berlin Fan Festival
items.content:
Today, Square Enix held the first day of Berlin's Final Fantasy XIV Fan Fest. They showed an extended look at the cinematic for Evercold, revealed the Bastion job, and more.

The new job revealed, Bastion, is a tank that wields a pair of greatshields called skyltborg. The shields are used to punch in one configuration, and shoot with another mode.

Evercold will also mark a shift in the game's narrative structure, allowing players a bit more freedom with different paths through the man scenario. Presumably, this will allow you to tackle different areas in the expansion in any order you wish. The new Auto Content Balancing will scale levels and difficulty to accommodate this.

We also got a look at Character Action Skins, a feature that lets players assign alternative animations to General actions like Teleport and Return. Additional skins for job actions will be coming in future updates. To help your Warrior of Light stand out, character customization will also be expanded with a new color picker, the ability to fine tune features like eyes and lips, new makeup options like eye shadow, and more.

We also got more info on the Evangelion crossover raid series, Ghosts of Desire, which you can view in the above trailer. Director and animator Mahiro Maeda is joining the project as a special guest artist and designer.

The new 8 man raid series in Evercold is also a crossover, this time themed around Final Fantasy VII, titled Beyond the Lifestream. The Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy VII Remake Project teams are working closely together to develop this.

The Nintendo Switch 2 version is now available for pre-order and will launch on August 4th with a one-month free subscription period. The Free Trial, Starter Edition, and Complete Editions will also be available.

There are a few technical changes coming as well, with an overhaul of the chocobo raising system, including the ability to call them in dungeons, and Same-Region Player Matching. Rather than being limited by logical data centers, players in the same general region will be able to play together more easily. This is coming to Japan in mid-October with other regions to follow.

Finally, we got a look at the Evercold Collector's Bundle, which includes a special box, a Reaper figure, an Ethos Metal Keychain, a Köttr Mini Plush, and a Tapestry of the Fourth. As of writing the Day 1 stream is still ongoing, and you can catch up on YouTube via this link .

For more on all things Final Fantasy XIV, stay tuned to GamingTrend.

items.title: FFXIV Evercold's new tank class Bastion is a big first for Final Fantasy
items.summary: Forget Gunbreakers. We've got Gunshields now
items.content:
By Josh Broadwell Published Jul 25, 2026, 11:39 AM EDT News Forget Gunbreakers. We've got Gunshields now

Image: Square Enix Square Enix producer Naoki Yoshida revealed Bastion, Final Fantasy 14 Evercold 's new tank class, during Fan Fest Berlin on Saturday, and it's a pretty big deal for Final Fantasy. Bastion is a main tank, a term introduced as part of FF14 's new "evolved" combat system that designates a tank as defense- and offense-oriented, rather than support-minded. And it's also the first brand-new class unassociated with any previous Final Fantasy job in FF14 .

The Bastion wields two special shields called Skyltborg, models of which Yoshida brought on stage during the address while wearing full Bastion garb (and quickly discarded thanks to their weight). These heavy shields represent a tradition of martial training on The Fourth ( Evercold 's setting) that stretches back generations, originating in a northern archipelago and passed down to those who dedicated their lives to protecting the realm. They're not just big shields, though. The Bastion's shields are shape-changing, aether-powered turrets that function as defensive devices and artillery units.

"Main tank" might mean defense first, but the Bastion does pretty much everything. Yoshida played a brief trailer showing the Bastion in action against one of Evercold 's big new enemies. The trailer showed no skill names, but you can see the Bastion going through several ability chains: One that creates a magic shield around the player, another that fires off aether-charged shots from a distance after charging for a few levels, a skill that makes the earth quake under an enemy, and an up-close melee combo chain. The Bastion also gets a set of "curative boons," though the trailer didn't show any of those.

Square Enix isn't in the habit of making new job roles in any Final Fantasy game, so Bastion is kind of a big deal. Even spinoffs like Brave Exvius (soon to be Final Fantasy Resonance ) repurpose older roles like FF12 's Green Mage and the Spellblade from FF5 . That's the philosophy Square Enix previously adopted with FF14 as well. Prior to Evercold , all of FF14 's job classes had ties to established roles in previous Final Fantasy games — obvious ones like Red Mage and Bard and some slightly more obscure references, like Reaper being a nod to Sice from Final Fantasy Type-0 and Final Fantasy 11 's scythe-wielding Dark Knight. Bastion has no such reference point. It's a totally fresh class designed with Evercold 's Evolved Combat in mind.

items.content:
Earlier this year, Square Enix announced Final Fantasy XIV Online would be making its way to the Switch 2 in August.

Now, in an update , it has confirmed its MMORPG will be launching for Nintendo's new hybrid system on 4th August 2026 . Pre-orders are now available for the following versions on the Switch 2 eShop. There's currently a pre-order discount on select versions.

There will also be the Final Fantasy XIV Online Free Trial . As for game download, the estimated file size is listed as 117GB .

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival in Berlin reveals the new tank job, new areas, and a new FFVII raid
items.summary: The middle is the hardest place to be for a Final Fantasy XIV fan festival. After all, director and producer Naoki Yoshida has to reveal a whole bunch of elements of the expansion, but we also need further reveals to be teased until the final fan festival occurs. Sometimes that means there isn't a whole lot [...]
items.content:
The middle is the hardest place to be for a Final Fantasy XIV fan festival. After all, director and producer Naoki Yoshida has to reveal a whole bunch of elements of the expansion, but we also need further reveals to be teased until the final fan festival occurs. Sometimes that means there isn’t a whole lot to say, but this particular fan festival was certainly not lacking for reveals, and they started right from the moment Yoshida walked on-stage in his full new job costume, as he always does.

While he was stacked in armor with a pair of shields strapped to his arms, of course he didn’t start off immediately by announcing the name of the job; instead, it started off with our new extended teaser. And like all extended teasers, we got our glimpse of one new job therein as well as a better picture of what will be happening in the expansion before more reveals started to fly fast and furious. Like the setting for most of the expansion, in fact.

Yoshida immediately explained that the airships we see are known as “Realmships” and will, in fact, be the setting for much of the expansion; there are five of them, known as the Five Firmaments, including the two we saw in the extended teaser as Naglfar (the Realmship of Water) and Hringhorni (the Realmship of Fire). But that was just a small tease before later previews, since Yoshida knew (correctly) that everyone was focused on the new job.

The new tank is Bastion, a main tank only available in Evolved mode, which starts at level 90 and is unlocked in Limsa Lominsa. While players have referred to the weapons as “gunshields” for years, they’re referred to as “skyltborgs,” paired shields that appear to flip between the punchy part and the gun part.

Originally, the job hails from Aerslant, the archipelago in the far north where Roegadyn originate from. The ancient martial techniques come from the archipelago’s rulers, offering both protection for allies and offensive options using aetherial artillery to stop raiders in their tracks. And true to form, there is video of the new job in action.

Our next job reveal, naturally, will be from the final festival in October. More about the story will also be revealed when the second part of the MSQ hits with patch 7.56, landing on September 8th. But there was still plenty to preview in terms of zones, and we got a look at three of them, both the overfield zones of Naglfar and Hringhorni as well as the first of the player towns located on the Naglfar, Fargarth.

While all three have new music, Yoshida was quick to point out that the new music may not be the music for the zones in the final version; Fargarth in particular was a temp track assembled by Soken in a single night. We also know that the big crystals are referred to as the Ark Crystals, although how they work will have to remain a mystery until we see the actual story.

Other zones were also shown off themed according to the remaining elements, but they weren’t yet named; however, it’s a clear theme. We also got a look at a variety of dungeons that are still in development but have not been given names just yet. And seeing the zones actually provides a fine segue into talking about main scenario changes, which are meant to offer players a wider variety of branching narratives.

For more or less all of FFXIV’s main scenario, you have a point or two of branching choice, but more often than not it’s between two zones that you can take on in either order very early in the MSQ. Evercold aims to have a wider branching field, with players able to pick between a larger number of different field areas and even dungeons to take on during their initial run of the quest.

In order to handle levels appropriately, the development team is introducing an auto content balancing system for a handful of dungeons and field areas, which is being added in a few places now but gives options for further content in the future. It’s not a full level scaling system for the open world, from the sound of it (it’s restricted to the MSQ specifically, for one thing) but it should provide more branching options on a whole.

From here, we moved on to talking more about the character animation overrides. As Yoshida explained, emotes and general actions are also character actions that can be overridden as well, with the idea being that you can customize multiple areas of character creation. He showed off three different potential teleport animations, and explained that the system will start with general action skins in 8.0, followed by the first round of job actions in 8.1. He also cautions that players will need to be patient, as these options take time to produce.

Similarly, 8.1 will feature more improved character creation options, including a toggle option for the darkening of Viera and Lalafell noses as well as Miqo’te face paint. And perhaps more significantly, Au Ra horns will be separated from face style. More is still coming, although Yoshida declined to explain more at this time. (Butt slider? Be patient!)

Moving forward, Yoshida also revealed the plan to bring what’s being called “world raids” to the field areas; it’s a working title, but the idea is to bring more field operation-style content to the open world. There’s also a system of automatic movement being planned for auto-moving to quest objectives.

Also, as mentioned in the first fan festival, a third difficulty is being added for normal raids between Normal and Savage. The targeted difficulty is somewhere around the Extreme raids, and the new raids will offer “season” gear as a mid-step between the difficulties. It’s meant to be a new option for players who want more practice with a mid-tier option. (Whether or not it will be available for queues was not discussed.)

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 reveals Nintendo Switch 2 release date and pricing, Final Fantasy 7 remake collaboration, more
items.summary: At the 2026 Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Berlin today, Square Enix revealed the release date for the MMORPG on Nintendo Switch 2. It will be out on August 4, 2026. Here’s the lineup of pricing: Starter Edition – $19.99 Complete Edition – $59.99 ($41.99 with pre-orders) Complete Collector’s Edition – $139.99 ($97.99 with pre-orders) Dawntrail Expansion (requires base...
items.content:
At the 2026 Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Berlin today, Square Enix revealed the release date for the MMORPG on Nintendo Switch 2. It will be out on August 4, 2026.

That was just one piece of news we got today. Square Enix also unveiled a Final Fantasy 7 Remake Trilogy crossover raid series and more.

Square Enix today revealed brand-new information about Evercold, the sixth expansion for its critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy 14 Online, set to launch in January 2027 alongside new playable content, a Final Fantasy 7 Remake Trilogy crossover raid series, the Nintendo Switch 2 version release date and more.

An extended teaser trailer for Evercold was also revealed, providing a glimpse into the world of the Fourth and the adventures that await the Warrior of Light in the start of the Goddless Realms Saga story arc.

During the Fan Festival 2026 in Berlin keynote address, Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida revealed the first new job coming to Evercold: Bastion—a main tank that wields a pair of greatshields known as skyltborg—and unveiled a trailer showcasing the new job in action.

Details were also shared on several new features coming to Evercold, including changes to the narrative structure that will be implemented for the main scenario, field, and game system, allowing players more freedom to choose what area they complete first between various paths in the main scenario. Through Auto Content Balancing, difficulty scaling and enemy levels will adjust to the appropriate player level as they play through dungeons in their chosen order. Additionally, a first look was provided for Character Action Skins, a feature that lets players assign alternate animations to personalize existing General actions, such as Teleport and Warp, with support for additional skins such as job actions arriving in future updates. Character customization will also be expanded so players have more ways to make their character stand out, including a greater range of color options with the new color picker, the ability to fine-tune features such as eyes and lips, new elements such as eye shadow, and more.

Following the reveal of the EVANGELION – Ghosts of Desire alliance raid series in April, Yoshida unveiled a new teaser trailer and announced that acclaimed director and animator Mahiro Maeda will join the project as a special guest artist and designer. Throughout his career, Maeda has contributed to numerous acclaimed projects, including “Mad Max: Fury Road” (2015) as a concept artist and designer, and “EVANGELION:3.0 +1.0 THRICE UPON A TIME” (2021), where he served as director, concept art director, storyboard artist, art setting designer and key animator.

Joined on stage by Final Fantasy 7 Remake series Director Naoki Hamaguchi, Yoshida also revealed “Beyond the Lifestream,” a new Final Fantasy 7-themed 8-player raid series that players will challenge in Evercold. Both development teams are working closely together to create an exciting new raid experience for players.

Further, Final Fantasy 14 will launch on Nintendo Switch 2 on Tuesday, August 4, 2026, with pre-orders starting today on Nintendo eShop. To ensure server stability, there will be an approximately one-month free subscription period on Nintendo Switch 2. Whether beginning with the Free Trial, starting their adventure with the Starter Edition, or diving into the full story and experience with the Complete Edition, more players than ever before will soon be able to join together in the vast world of Final Fantasy 14.

An outline of the content reveals from the keynote address can be found below:

Finally, Yoshida revealed the Evercold Collector’s Bundle, which includes a collection of physical items: the Evercold Special Art Box, Expertly Crafted Reaper Figure, Ethos Metal Keychain, Köttr Mini Plush, and Tapestry of the Fourth. Also included is the digital Collector’s Edition, featuring three in-game items: the Crystal Skyltborg bastion weapon, Vallhallar Odin mount, and Entreat Crystal emote. More information regarding availability and pre-orders will be announced in the future.

We’ve included trailers for what was shown off today below.
